Tech reviews should know this kind of stuff.

Regardless of what reviewers say, this card is going to end up being the replacement for the RX480/RX580 that everyone was looking for. The price point that the card is at is due to supply constraints on parts. This is not an upgrade for path for a 5700, nor should it ever have been as it's technically a step lower in the hirearchy of GPUs (X600 vs X700). I don't know many people that went from a GTX 670 to a GTX 760 and were happy with their "upgrade" as it's non-sensical to do so. The PC builders are being emotional and stressing out over something that even the manufacturers of the cards can't control. Look at the situation for what it is, not what you want it to be. It's not like this new generation of cards is worse than the previous gen, and the prices aren't much higher considering that it costs AMD more to produce, and also considering that the USD is worth less than it was when the Navi launched, it's a given that prices will go up. To complain about the prices of this card, and then completely ignore the fact that you can't get 3060s ANYWHERE for its MSRP (MAYBE nvidias website if you pay for a bot (which adds on to the overall cost of the card) is ridiculous to say the least. text: @nxn9172  At 1080p the 6600xt and 5700xt trade blows. The 5700xt pulls away at higher resolutions such as 1440p due to its memory subsystem having a 256bit bus compared to the 6600xt becoming starved of memory bandwidth with only a 128 bit bus and small cache. The RDNA2 architecture of the 6600xt struggles hard once at these higher resolutions because the cache becomes too small to shuffle larger blocks of data around leaving the 128 bits of memory bandwidth to the external GDDR6 in a brute force ‘bit blasting’ state where data that can’t fit in the cache is rapidly being paged in and out of the cache and main memory. This completely breaks the efficiency of the RDNA2 architecture of the 6600xt and the shear bandwidth advantage of the 5700xt takes hold to be victorious at higher resolutions.
